info.title: gim-hub client API
info.description:
Client API of the gim hub, the delivery service for MLS (RFC 9420) end-to-end encrypted IM clients. The hub stores and fans out opaque MLS messages and encrypted blobs and never sees plaintext or keys.

JSON fields are snake_case, timestamps are integer milliseconds since the Unix epoch, binary values are standard base64. Identity objects (DeviceList, AuthChallenge, recovery backup, link bundle) are gim-core CBOR wire formats carried as opaque base64 strings. User and device IDs are opaque strings whose format is owned by gim-core. Every non-2xx JSON response has the shape `{"error":{"code","message"}}`.

post.description: Issues a single-use gim-core AuthChallenge (audience = this hub's `hub_id`, 32-byte random nonce, valid for 5 minutes) for a device listed as active in the user's stored DeviceList. The device signs the challenge bytes into an AuthResponse and answers with POST /v2/auth/session before `expires_at`.

400.description: Malformed body, user ID or device ID (`validation_failed`)

404.description: No DeviceList stored for the user, or the device is not active in it (`not_found`)

post.summary: Answer a challenge and obtain a device token
post.description: Verifies the gim-core AuthResponse against the user's stored DeviceList and this hub's `hub_id`, then consumes the challenge: its nonce must have been issued by this hub for the same user and device, be unexpired and unused. The device must still be active (not revoked). The token is revoked when a later DeviceList revokes the device.

401.description: Unknown, used or expired challenge, or one issued by another hub or for another device (`invalid_challenge`); bad signature (`invalid_signature`); device revoked or not in the DeviceList (`device_not_active`)

post.description: Stores the request body verbatim. The client encrypts before upload and shares the blob ID and key inside MLS messages. Bodies larger than the hub limit (default 104857600 bytes) fail with 413.

get.description: Supports a single byte range (`Range: bytes=a-b`, `bytes=a-`, or `bytes=-n`).

Returns events addressed to the calling device with `cursor` greater than the given one, ascending. With `wait > 0` and no pending events the request is held open up to `wait` seconds until an event arrives.

If events after `cursor` have been pruned the hub responds 410 `cursor_expired` with the current head `cursor`; the client must resync (GET /v2/groups, message history, DeviceLists) and continue from that cursor.

After a wait the session is checked again: if it was deleted, expired or its device was revoked in the meantime the hub responds 401 `unauthorized` instead of returning events.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Last cursor the client has processed.

410.description: Cursor is older than the retention window (`cursor_expired`)

get.summary: List groups the calling device is a member of

post.description: Assigns a new `gid = <owner hub_id>/<random_128 base32lower>` (this hub's `hub_id`, stable across runtime-key rotation) at epoch 0 with the calling device as the only member. Further members are added by Commits.

403.description: Caller is not a member of the group (`not_member`)

post.summary: Submit an MLS Commit or Proposal
post.description:
`mls_message` is an MLS PublicMessage (Commit or Proposal), so the hub can parse it. The hub reads the epoch from the MLS framing (there is no client epoch field) and accepts the Commit only for the group's current epoch, advancing it by one. Membership changes are derived from the Add/Remove/Update proposals, carried by value or referenced (ProposalRef) from Proposals sequenced in the same epoch (an unknown reference fails with 400); each added member's gim-core credential (type 0xF001) is validated against their DeviceList, members are identified by user ID + device ID from their credentials, and `group.member_added` / `group.member_removed` events carry the `user_id`. The optional Welcome is delivered as a `welcome` event to `welcome_recipients`.

A Proposal (Add, Remove, SelfRemove or Update) must be for the current epoch; the hub sequences it and delivers it as a `message` of kind `proposal`, without changing the epoch or the roster: a later Commit that references it does. The result carries the Proposal's `seq` and the unchanged `epoch`; a Welcome is not allowed. Proposals of an epoch can no longer be referenced once the epoch advances.

Resubmitting the same Commit or Proposal (same hash) returns the original result with `duplicate: true` and emits nothing. Any other Commit or Proposal for a past epoch fails with 409 `stale_epoch`.

For a group owned by another hub (federation), this hub forwards the Commit or Proposal to the owning hub, which sequences it; the response is the owner's result and the local replica already holds the message. Added members on other hubs get their Welcome through their own hub. This needs the caller's hosting record listing this hub (403 `hosting_record_required`); when the owning hub refuses the request the result is 502 `peer_refused`, when it cannot be reached 503 `peer_unavailable` with `Retry-After` (retry the same Commit: it is idempotent by hash).

200.description: Duplicate of an accepted Commit or Proposal (`duplicate: true`)

400.description: Not a PublicMessage Commit/Proposal for this group, unknown proposal reference, invalid credential of an added member or of the sender's leaf, `welcome` not an MLSMessage carrying a Welcome, or Welcome fields inconsistent (`validation_failed`)

403.description: Caller is not a member of the group (`not_member`), group policy forbids the change (`forbidden`), or the group is owned by another hub and the caller has no valid hosting record listing this hub (`hosting_record_required`)

409.description: Commit or Proposal epoch is not the group epoch (`stale_epoch`)

502.description: The owning hub of the group refused the request (`peer_refused`)

503.description: The owning hub of the group is unreachable (`peer_unavailable`); retry after `Retry-After` seconds

get.description: Commits, Proposals and application messages with `seq >= from_seq`, ascending. For a group owned by another hub (federation), this hub serves its replica, which holds the log from the Commit that added this hub's first member on: a lower `from_seq` returns messages starting there.

403.description: Caller is not a member of the group (`not_member`)

post.description:
Stores the opaque MLS message, assigns the next `seq` and emits a `message` event to every member device except the sender. The epoch is read from the MLS framing; a message for another epoch fails with 409 `stale_epoch`.

Resending the same `client_id` from the same device returns the stored message with 200 and emits nothing. A decoded message larger than the hub limit (default 262144 bytes) fails with 413.

For a group owned by another hub (federation), this hub forwards the message to the owning hub, which assigns the `seq`; the response is the sequenced message. This needs the caller's hosting record listing this hub (403 `hosting_record_required`); when the owning hub refuses the request the result is 502 `peer_refused`, when it cannot be reached 503 `peer_unavailable` with `Retry-After` (retry with the same `client_id`).

200.description: Idempotent replay: the message stored earlier for this client_id

403.description: Caller is not a member of the group (`not_member`), or the group is owned by another hub and the caller has no valid hosting record listing this hub (`hosting_record_required`)

409.description: Message epoch is not the group epoch (`stale_epoch`)

502.description: The owning hub of the group refused the request (`peer_refused`)

503.description: The owning hub of the group is unreachable (`peer_unavailable`); retry after `Retry-After` seconds

put.summary: Claim a handle for the calling user
put.description: Optional per-hub directory mapping a handle to a user ID. Handles are never used as federation (DHT) keys. A user holds at most one handle per hub; claiming a new one releases the previous one. Re-claiming the caller's own handle is a no-op.

get.description: Unauthenticated. Lets a client check that a URL belongs to the `hub_id` listed in its hosting record before signing in.

post.summary: Upload KeyPackages for the calling device
post.description: Adds one-time KeyPackages, or with `last_resort: true` replaces the device's last-resort KeyPackage (exactly one package). Each hub of a multi-homed user holds its own disjoint set. Every leaf must carry the calling device's gim-core credential (type 0xF001), valid against the caller's stored DeviceList, with the certified device key as its signature key; otherwise the whole upload is rejected. A KeyPackage is uploaded to at most one hub, ever: an upload containing a KeyPackage this hub already claimed from another hub on a client's behalf is rejected as a whole.

400.description: Malformed or invalid KeyPackage, or invalid credential (`validation_failed`)

409.description: A KeyPackage was already claimed from another hub through this hub (`duplicate_key_package`)

post.summary: Claim one KeyPackage per active device
post.description:
For each target, atomically removes and returns one one-time KeyPackage per active device of the user's DeviceList (or only the given device). The device's last-resort KeyPackage is returned (and kept) only when its one-time packages are exhausted. Emits `keypackages.low` to a device whose one-time count drops below the threshold.

With federation, a target hosted on other hubs (per its hosting record) is claimed from its listed hubs in `(priority, hub_id)` order on the caller's behalf, moving to the next hub when one is unavailable or has no package; devices the first answering hub did not return are requested from the following hubs. Targets for which no hub answered and a hub could not be reached, refused or timed out are listed in `unavailable` (retryable). Claiming from another hub requires the caller to have a valid hosting record listing this hub. Claim and commit through the same hub.

403.description: A target is on another hub and the caller has no valid hosting record listing this hub (`hosting_record_required`)

post.description: Called by an existing device after scanning the new device's QR code. The bundle is relayed opaquely, kept for `expires_in` seconds (at most 600), and deleted on the first successful fetch. At most 262144 decoded bytes.

get.description: No authentication: the new device has no token yet; the bundle is sealed to its ephemeral key. With `wait > 0` and no bundle yet, the request is held open up to `wait` seconds. The bundle is deleted when returned; expired or already fetched bundles are 404.

parameters.name: link_id
parameters.description: Link ID from the QR code

404.description: No bundle within the wait time (`not_found`)

get.summary: Get the calling user and device

put.summary: Register the calling device for push
put.description: Replaces the calling device's push registration. `unifiedpush` requires `p256dh` and `auth` (RFC 8291 encryption keys); other providers ignore them.

delete.summary: Remove the calling device's push registration

get.description:
WebSocket upgrade delivering the same events as GET /v2/events in real time. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or, where headers cannot be set, `?token=`.

After the upgrade the hub first replays every event after `cursor`, then pushes new ones. Server-to-client frames are JSON text frames:

- `{"type":"event","event":Event}` - one per event, ascending `cursor`.
- `{"type":"error","error":{"code":"cursor_expired","message":"..."},"cursor":<head cursor>}` - sent when `cursor` is older than the retention window, followed by close code 4410. Resync, then reconnect with the given cursor.

An invalid or missing token closes the connection with code 4401. The session is checked again with every batch of events and at least every 30 seconds; once it is deleted, expires or its device is revoked by a DeviceList update, no further events are sent and the connection is closed with code 4401. Client-to-server frames are ignored.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Last cursor the client has processed.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Bearer token (alternative to the Authorization header).

101.description: Switching Protocols; frames as described above

get.description: No authentication (a bearer token, if sent, is ignored); returns only public data: the self-certifying DeviceList and the handle. Rate limited per client IP and per `user_id`, shared with `GET /v2/users/{user_id}/device-list`. For a user of another hub, the DeviceList comes from the cache of remote DeviceLists (fetched from the user's hub when missing or stale) and `handle` is absent.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Opaque user ID (format owned by gim-core)

429.description: Over the per-client-IP or per-user limit of unauthenticated reads (`rate_limited`); retry after `Retry-After` seconds

503.description: The user's hub is unreachable and no cached copy exists (`peer_unavailable`); retry after `Retry-After` seconds

get.description: No authentication (a bearer token, if sent, is ignored): the DeviceList is self-certifying public data, and a device restoring from a recovery code reads it before it can sign in. Rate limited per client IP and per `user_id`, shared with `GET /v2/users/{user_id}`. For a user of another hub, the hub answers from its cache of remote DeviceLists, fetching the list from the user's hub when it is not cached or older than `GIM_HUB_DEVICE_LIST_CACHE_HOURS`. A stale cached copy is returned if the user's hub cannot be reached.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Opaque user ID (format owned by gim-core)

429.description: Over the per-client-IP or per-user limit of unauthenticated reads (`rate_limited`); retry after `Retry-After` seconds

503.description: The user's hub is unreachable and no cached copy exists (`peer_unavailable`); retry after `Retry-After` seconds

put.description: No authentication: the DeviceList is self-certifying. The hub verifies the root key signature and that the list's user ID matches `user_id` (derived from the root key). The first upload creates the user on this hub. A later upload with a higher `seq` replaces the stored list; re-uploading the identical list (same `seq`, same bytes) is idempotent and returns 200. Devices revoked by the new list lose their tokens; a `device_list.updated` event is emitted to the user's other active devices and to every active device of users sharing a group with them. With federation, a replaced list of a hosted user is pushed to the hubs sharing groups with the user, which emit `device_list.updated` to their users in those groups.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Opaque user ID (format owned by gim-core)

200.description: DeviceList replaced, or identical to the stored one

400.description: Malformed or invalid DeviceList, or user ID mismatch (`invalid_device_list`)

409.description: `seq` is lower than the stored DeviceList, or equal with different bytes (`stale_device_list`)

post.summary: Get this hub's signed hosting entry for the caller
post.description: The hub co-signs its `HostingEntry` for the caller's user with its root key. The client puts the entry into its `SignedHostingRecord`, signs the record with the user root key and uploads it with `PUT /v2/users/{user_id}/hosting-record`. Signing is deterministic: repeated calls return identical bytes.

get.description: No authentication. For a user of this hub, the stored record; for any other user, the newest valid record resolved through federation (cached, fetched from the user's hubs or from the DHT). Rate limited per client IP and per `user_id`, sharing the budget of the other unauthenticated user reads (`GET /v2/users/{user_id}` and its `device-list`).

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Opaque user ID (format owned by gim-core)

429.description: Over the per-client-IP or per-user limit of unauthenticated reads (`rate_limited`); retry after `Retry-After` seconds

503.description: Resolution needed a peer hub that did not answer and the DHT had nothing (`peer_unavailable`, with `Retry-After` seconds)

put.summary: Upload the user's signed hosting record
put.description: No authentication: the record is self-certifying. Checks, in order: the record verifies for `user_id` (gim-core "Hosting record" verification; 400 `invalid_hosting_record` naming the gim-core error code); `user_id` is a user of this hub (404); the lifetime `expires_at - now` is between 1 hour and 30 days (400 `invalid_hosting_record`, `lifetime_out_of_range`); the seq rules against the stored record: a lower `seq`, or the same `seq` with a different body, is 409 `stale_hosting_record`, the identical record is 200 unchanged. A record listing this hub is published to the federation DHT. A record that does not list this hub is stored too; the hub then stops acting for the user in federation. With federation, a record that changes the listed hubs or priorities emits `hosting_record.updated` to the user's devices and is propagated to the user's other hubs, removed hubs and the hubs sharing groups with the user; a record that stops listing this hub removes the user here (writes refused with 403 `hosting_record_required`, data purged after `GIM_HUB_UNHOSTED_GRACE_HOURS`) until a later record lists it again.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Opaque user ID (format owned by gim-core)

200.description: Record replaced, or identical to the stored one

201.description: First record of the user stored

400.description: Invalid record, user ID mismatch or lifetime out of range (`invalid_hosting_record`), or malformed body (`validation_failed`)

404.description: Not a user of this hub (`not_found`)

409.description: `seq` is lower than the stored record, or equal with a different body (`stale_hosting_record`)

get.description: No authentication: this is the restore path of a user who lost every device. The backup is only useful with the recovery code. Requests are rate limited per client address and per `user_id` (429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`).

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Opaque user ID (format owned by gim-core)

put.description: Replaces the stored backup. Only the caller's own `user_id` is accepted. The backup is opaque ciphertext (gim-core recovery backup CBOR) of at most 65536 decoded bytes.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Opaque user ID (format owned by gim-core)

get.description: Welcomes addressed to the calling device that it has not acknowledged with POST /v2/welcomes/{gid}/ack, oldest first. Pending Welcomes are retained independently of event retention until acknowledged or the group is deleted, so after a 410 `cursor_expired` a client recovers group joins here instead of scanning history.

post.description: Marks the pending Welcome(s) for `gid` as processed for the calling device; they are no longer returned by GET /v2/welcomes/pending. Idempotent: returns 204 also when nothing is pending for `gid` (already acknowledged, or the group was deleted).

challenge.description:
gim-core AuthChallenge CBOR, base64. The device signs these exact
bytes into an AuthResponse as defined in gim-core docs/identity.md.

expires_at.description: When the challenge expires (ms since the Unix epoch, exclusive).

AuthChallengeRequest.description: Request a sign-in challenge for a device.

device_id.description: Opaque device ID (format owned by gim-core).

user_id.description: Opaque user ID (format owned by gim-core).

targets.description: Users or devices to claim one KeyPackage per active device for (1-100).

missing.description: Targets that are unknown, have no active device, or have no KeyPackage at all.

unavailable.description: Targets on another hub that could not be reached, refused, or timed out (retryable).

ClaimTarget.description: A user, or one device of a user.

device_id.description: Opaque device ID. Omit to target every active device in the user's DeviceList.

user_id.description: Opaque user ID (format owned by gim-core).

last_resort.description: True if this is the device's (reused) last-resort KeyPackage.

duplicate.description: True if this exact Commit or Proposal had already been accepted (nothing was emitted again).

epoch.description: Group epoch after the Commit; for a Proposal, the (unchanged) epoch it was sent in.

seq.description: Per-group sequence number of the Commit or Proposal.

priority.description: Priority of this hub in the record; lower is preferred.

CreateLinkBundleRequest.description: Post a sealed link bundle for a new device.

link_id.description:
Client-chosen random ID shared with the new device through the QR code
(16-64 chars of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _, -).

sealed_bundle.description:
gim-core link bundle CBOR sealed to the new device's ephemeral key,
base64. At most 262144 decoded bytes.

response.description:
gim-core AuthResponse CBOR, base64: the challenge bytes, user ID,
device ID and the device signature.

CursorExpiredError.description: 410 `cursor_expired`: events after the given cursor have been pruned.

cursor.description: Current head cursor; resync state, then continue from here.

user_id.description: Opaque user ID (format owned by gim-core).

DeviceListUpdatedEvent.description:
A newer DeviceList was stored for the receiving user or for a user sharing
a group with the receiving device.

Error.description: Body of every non-2xx JSON response.

Event.description: An entry of the calling device's event stream, ordered by `cursor`.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` in the next request (unchanged if no events were returned).

Group.description: A group as tracked by its delivery service.

epoch.description: Current MLS epoch (advanced by accepted Commits).

gid.description:
Group ID `<owner hub_id>/<random_128 base32lower>`, assigned by the hub. Clients use its
UTF-8 bytes as the MLS group ID.

last_seq.description: Highest assigned per-group sequence number (0 before the first message).

members.description: Member devices (delivery-service view of the roster).

GroupMember.description: A member device of a group.

user_id.description: Opaque user ID (format owned by gim-core).

HostingEntry.description: This hub's signed entry for the caller's hosting record.

entry.description:
gim-core CBOR `HostingEntry` `[hub_root_pubkey, priority, hub_sig]`,
base64; signing is deterministic, so repeated calls return identical
bytes.

hub_root_pubkey.description: The hub's 32-byte Ed25519 root public key, base64.

expires_at.description: Expiry of the record (ms since the Unix epoch, exclusive).

hosted.description: Whether the user is local to this hub and the record lists this hub.

HostingRecordExpiring.description: The receiving user's hosting record expires soon.

expires_at.description: When the stored record expires (ms since the Unix epoch).

HostingRecordExpiringEvent.description:
Emitted once per record `seq` (at most once per 24 hours per user) to the
user's active devices when less than 48 hours remain on the hosting
record listing this hub. Publish a renewed record (new `seq`).

HostingRecordHub.description: A hub entry of a hosting record.

HostingRecordUpdated.description: The receiving user's hosting record as stored by this hub.

expires_at.description: When the stored record expires (ms since the Unix epoch).

hosted.description: Whether the record lists this hub.

seq.description: `seq` of the stored record; dedup across hubs by it.

HostingRecordUpdatedEvent.description:
Emitted to the user's active devices on this hub when a stored record
changes the listed hubs or their priorities (renewals with the same
entries emit nothing). Multi-homing (H4), emitted with federation.

HubInfo.description:
This hub's identity, so a client can check that a URL belongs to the
`hub_id` listed in its hosting record before signing in.

hub_root_pubkey.description:
The hub's 32-byte Ed25519 root public key, base64; `hub_id` is
derived from it.

KeyPackageCount.description: KeyPackage stock of the calling device.

has_last_resort.description: Whether a last-resort KeyPackage is stored.

available.description: Remaining one-time KeyPackages of the receiving device.

sealed_bundle.description: gim-core link bundle CBOR sealed to the new device's ephemeral key, base64.

expires_at.description: When the bundle is deleted unless fetched first (ms since the Unix epoch).

device_id.description: Opaque device ID (format owned by gim-core).

handle.description: Handle claimed in this hub's directory, if any.

user_id.description: Opaque user ID (format owned by gim-core).

MembershipChange.description: Devices of one user added to or removed from a group by a Commit.

seq.description: Per-group sequence number of the Commit.

Message.description: An entry of a group's message log.

epoch.description: MLS epoch read from the message framing.

message_id.description:
Opaque message ID assigned by the owning hub, identical on every hub that stores the
message. Equals the push payload's `message_id` / `collapse_id`; the cross-hub dedup key.

seq.description: Per-group sequence number assigned by the owning hub, starting at 1.

MessageEvent.description:
A message (Commit or application) in a group the device is a member of.
Not delivered to the sending device.

cursor.description: Global event cursor of the receiving device.

has_more.description: True if more messages exist after the last returned one.

created_at.description: When the hub stored the Welcome.

PendingWelcome.description: A Welcome addressed to the calling device that it has not acknowledged.

PushRegistration.description: Push registration of the calling device.

app_id.description: APNs topic (app bundle ID) or FCM app ID; ignored by other providers.

auth.description:
UnifiedPush only (required there, ignored otherwise): the RFC 8291
authentication secret, base64url of 16 bytes.

p256dh.description:
UnifiedPush only (required there, ignored otherwise): the device's
RFC 8291 Web Push public key, base64url of the 65-byte uncompressed
P-256 point.

sandbox.description: APNs only: deliver through the sandbox environment.

token.description:
Provider token: APNs device token (hex), FCM registration token,
UnifiedPush endpoint URL, or any string for `log`.

device_list.description: gim-core DeviceList CBOR (`[tbs, sig]`, signed by the user root key), base64.

hosting_record.description:
gim-core CBOR `SignedHostingRecord`, base64, at most 8192 decoded
bytes.

backup.description:
gim-core recovery backup CBOR (root key encrypted under the
recovery-code key), base64. At most 65536 decoded bytes.

updated_at.description: When the backup was last stored (ms since the Unix epoch).

user_id.description: Opaque user ID (format owned by gim-core).

client_id.description: Sender-chosen idempotency key, unique per sending device and group (1-64 chars).

mls_message.description:
MLSMessage carrying a PrivateMessage (TLS encoding), base64. Content is never inspected; the
epoch is read from the framing.

expires_at.description: When the token expires (ms since the Unix epoch). Sign in again after.

token.description: Bearer token for this device. Returned once; store it securely.

StaleEpochError.description: 409 `stale_epoch`: the MLS message is not for the group's current epoch.

SubmitCommitRequest.description: Submit an MLS Commit or Proposal.

client_id.description: Sender-chosen idempotency key, unique per sending device and group (1-64 chars).

mls_message.description: MLSMessage carrying the Commit or Proposal as a PublicMessage (TLS encoding), base64.

ratchet_tree.description:
Ratchet tree for the new members (TLS encoding), base64, when it is not
carried in the Welcome as an extension.

welcome.description:
TLS-encoded MLSMessage (wire_format = mls_welcome) carrying the Welcome for the devices
added by this Commit, base64. Not allowed with a Proposal.

welcome_recipients.description: Devices the Welcome is addressed to (1-500). Required with `welcome`.

UploadKeyPackagesRequest.description: Upload KeyPackages for the calling device.

key_packages.description: Serialized MLS KeyPackages (TLS encoding), base64 each (1-100).

last_resort.description:
When true, `key_packages` must hold exactly one package, which replaces
the device's last-resort KeyPackage. Otherwise the packages are added
to the device's one-time pool.

User.description: A user as known to this hub.

handle.description: Handle claimed in this hub's directory, if any.

user_id.description: Opaque user ID (format owned by gim-core).

Welcome.description: An MLS Welcome addressed to the receiving device.

ratchet_tree.description: Ratchet tree (TLS encoding), base64, if the sender supplied one.

seq.description:
Per-group sequence number of the Commit that produced the Welcome;
fetch messages from `seq + 1` after joining.

welcome.description: TLS-encoded MLSMessage (wire_format = mls_welcome) carrying a Welcome, base64.
